children.topic: Gallbladder Carcinoma
Epidemiology: Most common biliary tract cancer, 5th GI cancer, F:M = 3:1, high incidence in Chile, Northern India, Native Americans
Risk Factors: Gallstones (>3cm 10x risk), Porcelain gallbladder (20% cancer risk), GB polyps (>10mm), Anomalous pancreaticobiliary junction (APBJ), Chronic Salmonella typhi infection
Pathology: Adenocarcinoma (90%), direct spread to liver (Segments IVb & V) and regional lymph nodes (porta hepatis)
Clinical Picture: Usually advanced at diagnosis. RUQ pain, weight loss, jaundice (indicates liver/biliary invasion)
Incidental GB Cancer (found post-cholecystectomy): T1a (lamina propria) = Cholecystectomy alone is curative; T1b+ (muscularis) = Radical re-resection (wedge liver resection IVb/V + lymphadenectomy)
Cholangiocarcinoma (Bile Duct Cancer)
Classification by Location:
Intrahepatic (10%): Peripheral liver parenchyma mass
Perihilar / Klatskin Tumor (50-60%): Junction of R & L hepatic ducts at confluence
Distal Extrahepatic (20-30%): Between upper border of pancreas and ampulla
Risk Factors: Primary Sclerosing Cholangitis (PSC - 10-15% lifetime risk), Choledochal cysts, Liver flukes (Clonorchis sinensis), Thorotrast exposure
Klatskin Tumor — Bismuth-Corlette Classification:
Type I: Tumor below hepatic duct confluence
Type II: Tumor involves confluence without involving R or L hepatic ducts
Type IIIa: Extends into Right hepatic duct; Type IIIb: Extends into Left hepatic duct
Type IV: Involves both Right & Left hepatic ducts or multicentric
Diagnosis & Markers: CA 19-9 (>100 U/mL), MRCP (gold standard non-invasive), EUS-FNA, ERCP with brush cytology
Surgical Management:
Perihilar (Klatskin): En bloc resection of extrahepatic bile duct + Hepatectomy (usually right) + Caudate lobectomy + Portal lymphadenectomy
Distal Extrahepatic: Pancreaticoduodenectomy (Whipple procedure)
Palliative: ERCP biliary stenting (metal stent) or PTBD to relieve jaundice & pruritus
